I’ve been told there are bugs with resource saving for which the little save button is a workaround. Ideally those should be addressed before merging this change. Would be great if folks who are running in to those bugs would comment on this PR with the issue reports or fixing PRs so that those can become a dependency.

As I mention on Bluesky, the issues with resources aren't exactly easy to report. Without knowing what's causing the save not to trigger when the project as a whole is saved, or by the auto-save before the debug run, such a report will be useless to maintainers. Without a reproduction a complaint like that will be low priority, as there is nothing to investigate unless you know where to look first.

So at this time I can't offer anything beyond that it happens, and resources do not always get saved as you expect them to. And the explicit save action on the resource is one sure way to guarantee that they do.

-----

Now, I'll repeat another thing I posted on Bluesky. What problems like this indicate is that the approach to editor changes should be focused on each individual exposed feature, rather than blanket changes. You should ask yourself:

- Why was this feature/action exposed to users in the first place?
- Is that reason still relevant today?
- Are there more reasons to expose this feature nowadays?
- Is that the best way to expose this feature, or could it be improved?

There is absolutely no reason to hastily try and remove elements you personally don't think are relevant to people. You don't know that yet. The latest proposal makes some heavy assumption that none of these features are commonly used (based on what?) and only advanced users benefit from them (and thus must suffer more to access them?). And that is its opening statement, given as a fact of the problem being present.

But it should be a discussion starter instead. A discussion that then delves into each exposed feature and its relevance. What is this obsession with "clean" and "simplified", without any research into what is used and how, what is necessary to be productive, and even yes, what may be a required workaround for some funky editor behavior? Of course people will thumbs-up and heart aesthetical changes. THEY ALWAYS DO. But that's not how UX should be judged and developed.

I thoroughly do not appreciate that instead of efforts into investigating the potentially problematic area (a hypothesis, not a truth statement) we have a proposal that insists on its claims, and now a PR that readily implements its ideas (with full endorsement of same maintainers). Instead of giving this a room for discussion this only solidifies this change as inevitable. Especially given how previous such discussions resulted in no major changes being even considered, and users who have problem with them being asked to compromise or deal with it.

That's it from me.

> I’ve been told there are bugs with resource saving for which the little save button is a workaround.

First time I hear about that. The editor automatically saves all external resources when you save a scene (i.e. use the "main" save option).

> First time I hear about that. The editor automatically saves all external resources when you save a scene (i.e. use the "main" save option).

Unfortunately, it doesn't reliably save resources that do not belong to any of the open scenes. Out of the issues that have been reported, there was one ticket, I recall, about theme resource changes not being reflected the next time you run your project.

But I, personally, also have it with other kinds (scripted, namely) of resources. I'm not yet sure how that happens as I haven't had time (or desire really) to dig deeper. Clicking the button is enough for me for now, to progress with my work.

I think the best place to discuss this would be on the proposal. The PR discussion should be reserved to technical discussions regarding the implementation, whereas the proposal serves as a ground for everyone to discuss problems and ideas to resolve them.

> I thoroughly do not appreciate that instead of efforts into investigating the potentially problematic area (a hypothesis, not a truth statement) we have a proposal that insists on its claims, and now a PR that readily implements its ideas (with full endorsement of same maintainers). Instead of giving this a room for discussion this only solidifies this change as inevitable. Especially given how previous such discussions resulted in no major changes being even considered, and users who have problem with them being asked to compromise or deal with it.

Just to clarify 2 things:
1. The proposal _is_ the room for discussion. Everyone is welcome to participate, voicing support or constructive criticism. Changes that affect many users will not be merged until they've had a healthy dose of discussion.
2. Support by people who happen to be maintainers is not the same as them endorsing it in their capacity as maintainers. I, for example, do like this change, but I wouldn't endorse it until I know if the community stands behind it or not.

All that is to say; this change is all but "inevitable"! Please participate in the discussions; the more people get involved and share how this would affect their workflows, the better!

> What is this obsession with "clean" and "simplified", without any research into what is used and how

Discussions about the inspector header started in RC where all of the maintainers are and where there's a higher chance to get an insight into why things were exposed.

https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/usability

Discussion about the inspector header buttons started specifically with me asking why some of them are exposed and whether anybody is using them:

https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/usability?msg=xyYB8Z8NrmPWGBZi8

Adriaan also made bluesky posts to gather more opinions. As Jayden said in the note above, this PR will change as necessary as we get more information. Godot doesn't have telemetry and we need to rely on asking around and thinking about features analytically, it's the best we can do with what we have. We're still thinking about ways to gather more opinions without flooding the community with surveys or relying on social media posts to go viral, because this is not the first and not the last UI change that godot will ever need.

This is an open-source project and everybody is welcome to join the discussion, both in the proposals like @Ivorforce suggested and on rocket chat where you can help us decide how best to approach UI/UX changes in general.

I find the exploration of all the variations in this PR confusing. Would be best if those variations are separate PRs, or mockups in a proposal. Like @passivestar said, we should double down on a design that reduces the clutter. I think the design from [April 10](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117499#issuecomment-4222220073) + the small fixes that were applied to it, were a good compromise where we cleaned up everything but add the save button when inspecting a resource. I'd avoid toolbar visibility toggles as much as possible.
Rebased.

> Tested, works as expected
> 
> Some feedback:
> 
> 1. The dedicated save button should just save instead of being a dropdown, otherwise it's the same 2 clicks as the menu. It's better for the hot path to be single click
> 2. The text of the object name in the header should be bold because it's more important than the section headers but has lower visual weight than them atm

Both done!

By the way: I wanted to note that this PR has the potential to interrupt the workflow of some users. I am of the opinion that merging it and getting feedback on it during alpha / dev is the best way forward. No functionality is lost and the overall readability of the inspector is improved with this PR, so I _think_ this PR is a net-positive for the average user… but opinions on that will vary. I tend to think that if we let too many concerns stop us from cleaning up the editor and making any changes, I just don't see a way forward to a cleaner UI.

This PR needs another usability review and a code review.
